Using your own gauge: USGS, Colorado DWR, or a csv file

Source: vignettes/your-flow-data.Rmd
your-flow-data.Rmd

The code in this vignette downloads data, so it is shown but not run when the package is built.

library(WSVAflowR)
options(wsva.data_dir = "~/flow_data")   # downloads and caches go here

Flow from any source

Every flow source returns the same table (daily date, q_cms, flag) plus metadata such as the station name, location and drainage area.

q <- flow_usgs("01154000")                      # USGS Water Data APIs (dataRetrieval)
q <- flow_cdss("CCACCRCO")                      # Colorado DWR / CDSS (cdssr)
q <- flow_from_csv("my_gauge.csv", date_col = "Date", q_col = "Flow_cfs", units = "cfs",
                   date_format = "%m/%d/%Y", id = "my_gauge", lon = -105.27, lat = 40.01)
q <- flow_from_df(my_data_frame, date_col = "date", q_col = "q", units = "cms")

Units can be "cfs", "cms" (m³/s) or "mm" (mm/day over the basin, which needs area_km2). Negative values are dropped, and missing days stay missing: nothing is gap-filled.

A watershed

wsva_basin() needs a watershed polygon. Give one, or let it delineate the watershed upstream of the gauge:

b <- wsva_basin(q)                       # delineate at the gauge location in the flow metadata
b <- wsva_basin(q, outlet = c(-105.27, 40.01))
b <- wsva_basin(q, polygon = sf::st_read("my_watershed.gpkg"))
b <- wsva_basin_usgs("01154000")         # USGS gauges: USGS flow + the NLDI basin for the site

Delineation uses USGS StreamStats (state elevation-derived flow networks), falling back to NHDPlus through the NLDI:

ws <- delineate_basin(-106.2776, 39.01826, method = "streamstats")

Always compare the watershed with a published drainage area. The flow is converted to mm/day with a reference area: the area in the flow metadata, else the GAGES-II or USGS area when the station has a USGS id, else the delineated area. wsva_basin() warns when the delineated area is more than 20% off; a large mismatch usually means the outlet snapped to the wrong stream.

Climate and basin attributes 

b <- add_forcing(b)                      # GridMET, 1980-10-01 to 2024-09-30 by default
b <- add_basin_attributes(b)
Attribute Source
Elevation, slope, aspect, hypsometry AWS Terrain Tiles (USGS 3DEP in the US) via elevatr
Soil water storage (WBM soil bucket) gNATSGO (SSURGO + STATSGO2) via soilDB; 0-150 cm by default
Rain/snow temperature threshold Jennings et al. (2018), shipped with the package
Land cover and crop coefficients NLCD 2019 via FedData

Potential evapotranspiration is never taken from a dataset’s own product: it is always computed from temperature, humidity, radiation and wind (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith × land-cover crop coefficient), so historical and projected climate go through one method.

Things to watch for

  • Human influence. Many state-operated gauges, including many Colorado DWR stations, sit below diversions or reservoirs. The models simulate natural flow, so water management shows up as model error. check_basin() reports the GAGES-II class when the station has a USGS id; otherwise you need to check.
  • Record length. Cross-validation needs at least two complete water years per fold (ten for the default five folds) inside the forcing period.
  • Seasonal records. Stations that only report in summer still work: scoring uses only observed days, and the models run on continuous forcing.
  • Coverage. GridMET covers the contiguous US.

Then fit 

check_basin(b)
fits <- fit_models(b)
summary(fits)
plot(fits)
saveRDS(fits, "my_gauge_fits.rds")
